title: Houdin's theory that the Great Pyramid was built from the inside out (internal ramp)
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Houdin's theory that the Great Pyramid was built from the inside out (internal ramp), about Fourth Dynasty, c. 2560 BC at Egypt (no place named), and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: Houdan in in in France saying that it was built from the inside out.

French architect Jean-Pierre Houdin suggests that an internal ramp spiraling within the pyramid structure itself carried the blocks. This is an idea that gained renewed interest after the Scan Pyramids project detected unexplained voids inside the Great Pyramid.
tellings.difference: Links the theory to the voids that ScanPyramids detected.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell Houdin's theory that the Great Pyramid was built from the inside, by an internal ramp.

as_told.title: Houdin's internal ramp theory and the ScanPyramids voids

tellings.quote: And you have people like I think Jean-Pierre Houdin in France who say that there is something about like, you know, internally like the blocks get pulled up or something.
tellings.difference: Describes the blocks being pulled up internally, where the story calls it building from the inside out.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell Jean-Pierre Houdin's theory that the Great Pyramid was built from the inside, with blocks moved up internally.

tellings.quote: I think one of the leading, you know, researchers on how it was built is a guy Jean-Pierre Houdin
tellings.difference: Adds talk of an older date for the pyramid alongside the ramp theory.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell Jean-Pierre Houdin's theory that the Great Pyramid was built from the inside out using an internal ramp.

as_told.title: Pyramid internal ramp theory and older dating

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, has talked several times about the ideas of Jean-Pierre Houdin, a French architect he calls a leading researcher on how the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt was built. As Michels tells it, Houdin thinks the pyramid was built from the inside out, with a ramp spiraling inside the structure that carried the blocks up. Michels links this to a project called ScanPyramids, which scanned the pyramid and found unexplained empty spaces inside, and in one telling he also brings up the idea that the pyramid may be older than usually thought.
